title: Help flag and flag-after-directory handling
description: The source defines exit 2 for unknown options but is silent on -h/--help and on options placed after the directory. Options after the directory would be extra arguments.

options.label: Treat -h/--help as an unknown option and options after the directory as extra arguments: exit 2
Print usage to stdout and exit 0 for help

title: Unreadable subdirectory during walk
description: Rule 6 covers unreadable files only. A subdirectory that cannot be listed could abort or be skipped.

options.label: Emit one stderr warning, skip it, keep exit code unchanged

title: Strictness of --min-size parsing
description: Positive integer is required. Forms such as +5, 0x10, 1e3, or values overflowing int64 are ambiguous.

options.label: Accept only ASCII decimal digits, value >= 1 and fitting int64; all else exit 2
Accept anything strconv.ParseInt accepts that is positive

title: Symlinked directory argument
description: cli resolves the directory with filepath.EvalSymlinks before walking so a symlink to a directory is walked; validation still uses os.Stat as specified.
system_choice: cli resolves the directory with filepath.EvalSymlinks before walking so a symlink to a directory is walked; validation still uses os.Stat as specified.

title: bin/test.sh logging
description: Output goes to data/logs/test_<stamp>.log and is printed after completion rather than streamed, because pipefail/tee exit-status handling is not POSIX. Acceptable?
system_choice: Output goes to data/logs/test_<stamp>.log and is printed after completion rather than streamed, because pipefail/tee exit-status handling is not POSIX. Acceptable?

title: Unreadable subdirectory warning
description: walk.Files emits one warning line per unreadable subdirectory and returns nil for it, so the walk continues. A failure to read the root itself is returned as an error (exit 1). Acceptable?
